# Development roadmap

Last reviewed 15 October 2026. **Ag-GIS is not release-ready.** This is the current direction, not a delivery-date or purchase promise. Existing experimental downloads do not change that status.

## Now: make the project understandable and contributable

- Clear canonical agent/contributor instructions, repository map and verifiable setup commands.
- Consistent repository logos and documented asset sources.
- Explicit user ownership, control, export, local operation and honest communication principles.
- Useful bug/idea forms, a PR checklist and basic CI that states its limits.
- Keep unfinished local features separate from the public base until deliberately integrated and checked.

## Next: improve the farmer workflow

- Prioritise a clear interface and understandable actions.
- Refine farm organisation and safe import placement with inspectable outcomes.
- Make save/reopen, cancellation, error recovery and plugin reload dependable.
- Prove a supported farming task can be completed without a setup/support call.

## Later: optional online services

- Backups with verified complete recovery and usable exports.
- Mobile/browser viewing of selected farm information.
- Focused field collection, sharing and conflict-safe desktop synchronisation.
- A separately costed hosted workspace/remote-desktop option.

These online services are not implemented or available for purchase. Local work must remain useful without a subscription. No cloud dependency, data sale or lock-in is a condition of participation.

## How people guide this

Start with a safe example and the farming task in [Ag-GIS Feedback](https://github.com/JamRov/Ag-GIS-Feedback/issues). Maintainers explain accepted, deferred and declined changes. Votes and commercial interest inform priorities; they do not override data integrity, user control or maintainability. Code/documentation changes are proposed through pull requests. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
